references.text: Rebekah warns Jacob of Esau's revenge plans and sends him to his brother Laban in Haran – the direct cause of Jacob's departure
Isaac blesses Jacob and sends him to Paddan-Aram to find a wife among Laban's daughters, which is the immediate occasion for his departure from Beersheba
God calls Abram to leave his home and go to a land He will show him, a parallel to Jacob's departure from Beersheba
God renews His promise to Isaac to give him and his descendants the land, which forms the background for Jacob's journey
Hosea refers to Jacob's flight to Aram (Haran) and the service he performed for a wife, pointing back to this journey
Jacob arrives in the Haran region and meets shepherds at the well – the direct continuation of the journey from Beersheba
Terah took his family from Ur and settled in Haran, providing geographical background for Jacob's destination
This is a direct continuation of the journey; 29:1 confirms that Jacob has reached his goal (the land to the east) which he set out for in 28:10.
Forms a narrative frame showing Jacob's journey from flight to safe return after receiving God's promise.
At Bethel, Jacob had his first vision (after departing in 28:10); arriving here confirms that God has accompanied him all the way from Haran back to the place of promise.
Thematic parallel: Both patriarchs show obedience by leaving their homes and going where God leads them.
Contrast between Jacob's flight from Be'er-Sheba and Isaac's safe arrival there; shows God's guidance in different life stages.
